368142.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). Everything below is at the same location, called {Location-A} (for example "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"), shown in the top bar next to the bell.
  • The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  • A desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher).
  • Three eligible technicians at {Location-A}: {Technician-A} (for example "Jenny Wilson"), {Technician-B} (for example "Ralph Edwards") and {Technician-C} (for example "Dana Ortiz"); use exactly these names, because the expected results name them. A technician is eligible when Time Clock is on, the staff member is active (not deactivated), the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and {Location-A} is picked in their Location field.
  • A customer used by this case only, with one contact and one asset, called {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Scheduled Techs Lines").
  • A work order for {Customer-A}, called {Work-order-A}: status Approved, no lead technician, and three lines approved for repair, none with a labor technician, called {Line-A}, {Line-B} and {Line-C} (for example any ready-made lines such as "Replace - Brake pot").
  • Schedule shifts on {Work-order-A} tomorrow: {Technician-A} 8:00–10:00 on {Line-B}; {Technician-B} 10:00–12:00 on {Line-C}; {Technician-C} 13:00–15:00 on {Line-C}. {Line-A} has no shift.
368142.custom_steps:
1. Open {Work-order-A} and click the Lines tab.
  2. Look at {Line-B}'s Labor row.
  3. Look at {Line-C}'s Labor row.
  4. Look at the {Line-B} and {Line-C} rows for any badge (for example "Needs techs").
368142.expected_head:
Expected results

  • Step 2: {Line-B}'s Labor row shows {Technician-A}'s name in place of "Unassigned".
  • Step 3: {Line-C}'s Labor row shows both scheduled technicians, {Technician-B} and {Technician-C} (2 names).
  • Step 4: Neither row shows a "Needs techs" badge or any other badge.
368142.moved: Setup block (7 steps: staff check, customer/contact/asset, work order with 3 approved lines, 3 Schedule shifts, setup check) -> doc Part 1 (30 steps) and Part 2; Needs line and Build line removed; window width, role/permission, location, technician eligibility kept as bullets; [WO-1]->{Work-order-A}, [Cust-1]->{Customer-A}, Line 1/2/3->{Line-A/B/C}, named technicians->{Technician-A/B/C} with "use exactly these names".

  4. Look at {Line-A}'s Story row and the line row again.
96997.expected_head:

  • Steps 2 and 4: {Line-A} shows its story text with no check-mark indicator anywhere on the line, on the normal work order page and in the Simple Flow tech view mode.

96998.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). Everything below is at the same location, called {Location-A} (for example "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"), shown in the top bar next to the bell.
  • The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  • A customer used by this case only, with one contact and one asset, called {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Story Entry").
  • A work order for {Customer-A}, called {Work-order-A}, with status Approved, a mileage entered on the work order, and two lines, called {Line-A} and {Line-B} (for example any ready-made lines such as "Replace - Brake pot"), neither with a tech story.
96998.custom_steps:
1. Open {Work-order-A} and click the Lines tab.
  2. Add a tech story to {Line-A} (for example "First note") and save it.
  3. Edit {Line-A}'s story to "First note, edited" and save it.
  4. Try to complete {Line-B}, which has no tech story.
  5. Add a tech story to {Line-B}.
  6. Complete {Line-B}.
96998.expected_head:
Expected results

  • Steps 2 and 3: Entering and editing the story work as before and the edited text shows.
  • Steps 4 to 6: Completing a line without a tech story is still blocked with today's message (a tech story is required), and works once the story is entered. Nothing else about tech stories changed; only the check mark is gone.
